enhanced.fullText:
Section 1557 of the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act (42 U.S.C. § 18116) serves as the primary federal civil rights law prohibiting discrimination on the basis of race, color, national origin, sex, age, or disability in covered health programs or activities. For higher education institutions, this regulation applies to any health-related program or activity that receives federal financial assistance, including student health centers, counseling services, health insurance plans, and health-related academic programs.

The statute incorporates enforcement mechanisms from Title IX of the Education Amendments of 1972 (20 U.S.C. § 1681), Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 (29 U.S.C. § 794), the Age Discrimination Act of 1975 (42 U.S.C. § 6101), and Title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 (42 U.S.C. § 2000d). Universities must ensure that individuals with disabilities receive effective communication through auxiliary aids and services, including qualified interpreters, assistive listening devices, large print materials, and accessible electronic formats as specified in 45 CFR § 92.202.

Key disability-related provisions require institutions to provide reasonable modifications to policies and procedures, ensure physical accessibility to facilities, and maintain accessible websites and digital platforms for health services. The regulation mandates that covered entities cannot exclude or deny services to individuals with disabilities, charge different fees, or provide services that are not as effective as those provided to others. Universities must designate a Section 1557 coordinator, conduct self-evaluations of current services and policies, and establish grievance procedures for disability-related complaints.

Enforcement authority rests with the Department of Health and Human Services Office for Civil Rights (HHS OCR), which can investigate complaints, conduct compliance reviews, and impose sanctions including termination of federal funding. The 2020 final rule (85 FR 37160) clarified that Section 1557 applies to health insurance coverage offered through university-sponsored plans and requires institutions to post notices of nondiscrimination in multiple languages. Violations can result in monetary penalties up to $19,639 per incident under 45 CFR § 92.603, with higher penalties for repeat violations. Private individuals may also file lawsuits seeking monetary damages and injunctive relief under 42 U.S.C. § 18116(a).
enhanced.summary: Section 1557 of the Affordable Care Act prohibits discrimination based on disability in university health programs receiving federal funding, requiring auxiliary aids, accessible facilities, and effective communication for students and employees with disabilities.
enhanced.requirements:
## Auxiliary Aids and Services
- Provide qualified interpreters, assistive listening devices, and accessible formats for health communications
- Ensure effective communication at no cost to individuals with disabilities
- Maintain updated inventory of available auxiliary aids per 45 CFR § 92.202

## Digital Accessibility Standards
- Implement WCAG 2.1 Level AA standards for all health-related websites and applications
- Ensure electronic health records and patient portals are fully accessible
- Provide alternative formats for digital health information

## Administrative Compliance
- Designate Section 1557 coordinator responsible for disability compliance
- Establish formal grievance procedures for discrimination complaints
- Conduct annual self-evaluation of policies and accessibility barriers
- Post nondiscrimination notices in multiple languages and formats

## Physical Accessibility
- Ensure health facilities meet ADA Accessibility Guidelines standards
- Provide accessible medical equipment and examination tables
- Maintain accessible parking and building entrances for health services
enhanced.reportingRequirements: Submit annual assurance of compliance to HHS OCR by December 31st. Report disability-related incidents or complaints within 30 days to institutional Section 1557 coordinator. Maintain documentation of auxiliary aid requests and accommodations for three years per 45 CFR § 92.701.
